1.title: Ingress
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Ingress. It covers the exam area Services and Networking. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. What Ingress adds to a Service. An Ingress object. Create one fast. T L S. Test and troubleshoot. Practice with six hands-on labs worth forty-five points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Services and Networking (twenty percent). Practice in this module: six labs, forty-five points, about forty-eight minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: What Ingress adds to a Service
1.text: What Ingress adds to a Service. The figure shows this: Ingress routing. Exam tip: An Ingress does nothing without a controller: set ingress Class Name and keep the backend Service in the same namespace.

1.title: What Ingress adds to a Service, continued
1.text: What Ingress adds to a Service. A Service of type Node Port or Load Balancer exposes one application per port or per address. An Ingress exposes many H T T P and H T T P S applications behind one entry point, and chooses the backend by the host name and the path of the request. Two parts work together. Ingress (the object). the rules: "host a dot example dot com goes to Service a ". Ingress controller (a program running in the cluster). reads the Ingress objects and does the routing (Traefik, nginx-based controllers, H A Proxy, cloud controllers).

1.title: What Ingress adds to a Service, continued
1.text: What Ingress adds to a Service. An Ingress does nothing without a controller. A controller serves only Ingresses that belong to its Ingress Class: spec dot ingress Class Name names the class. The C K A D environment already has a controller; read kube control get ingressclass to see the class name to use. (This course's labs use Traefik with the class traefik. The exam controller can differ: the objects are the same, only the class name changes.).

1.title: An Ingress object
1.text: An Ingress object. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: path Type is required, and the longest matching path wins.

1.title: An Ingress object, continued
1.text: An Ingress object. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: An Ingress object, continued
1.text: An Ingress object. host. the Host header of the request; without it the rule matches every host. path. the U R L path. path Type. required: Prefix ( slash api matches slash api and slash api slash x ), Exact (only that path), Implementation Specific (the controller decides). backend dot service. the Service name and port that receives the traffic. default Backend. where requests go that match no rule. tls. hosts and the Secret that holds the certificate (below). The backend Service is in the same namespace as the Ingress. The Ingress is only the rule: the Service must exist and have endpoints.

1.title: An Ingress object, continued
1.text: An Ingress object. Default backend. default Backend receives the requests that match no rule. Controllers differ in how they honor it next to host rules: on the Traefik test cluster it works reliably when it is the only setting of an Ingress of its own (a second Ingress holds the host rules), so test it with a request to an unknown host.

1.title: An Ingress object, continued
1.text: An Ingress object. Path matching. When several paths match, the longest wins: with slash api and or both present, slash api slash users goes to the slash api backend. A path rule does not rewrite the U R L: the backend still receives slash api slash users, so the app must serve that path (rewrites need a controller-specific annotation or middleware).

1.title: Create one fast
1.text: Create one fast. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: kube control create ingress builds the Ingress from the rule flag options; a path ending in a star is a Prefix.

1.title: Create one fast, continued
1.text: Create one fast. In the rule flag, a path ending in becomes Prefix; without it is Exact. For a default backend plus rules, generate yamel ( the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml ) and add default Backend.

1.title: TLS
1.text: T L S. H T T P S needs a certificate. Put the certificate and key in a T L S Secret, in the same namespace as the Ingress, and name it in tls. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Ingress T L S needs a Secret of type Kubernetes dot io slash tls in the same namespace as the Ingress.

1.title: TLS, continued
1.text: T L S. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: TLS, continued
1.text: T L S. The Secret must be of type Kubernetes dot io slash tls with the keys tls dot crt and tls dot key (a generic Secret with the same files is not accepted by controllers). The certificate's name should match the host.

1.title: Test and troubleshoot
1.text: Test and troubleshoot. Test from inside the cluster, with a Host header and without D N S: kube control run t the rm flag -it the restart flag set to Never the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six then the command W get -q O- the header flag Host a dot example dot com H T T P colon slash slash controller service. From a machine that can reach the controller: curl dash H Host a dot example dot com H T T P colon slash slash ip or. Exam tip: A four oh four for every request points to the wrong Ingress Class or host; a five oh three points to a Service without endpoints.

1.title: Test and troubleshoot, continued
1.text: Test and troubleshoot. four oh four from the controller for every request. Likely cause: no Ingress accepted for that host: wrong ingress Class Name (a class that no controller serves) or wrong host. Check: kube control get ingressclass, kube control get ingress dash o yaml. four oh four only for some paths. Likely cause: path or path Type does not match. Check: kube control describe ingress. five hundred two or five oh three from the controller. Likely cause: the backend Service has no endpoints, or the name or port is wrong. Check: kube control describe ingress (Backend line), kube control get endpoints. service x not found in the describe output. Likely cause: the backend Service name has a typo. Check: kube control get svc. Works with H T T P, certificate error with H T T P S. Likely cause: wrong Secret type, wrong namespace or a certificate for another host. Check: kube control get secret dash o yaml.

1.title: Test and troubleshoot, continued
1.text: Test and troubleshoot. Exam tip. Read the Ingress Class first: kube control get ingressclass. A task that gives you "the Ingress controller is installed" still expects ingress Class Name to be set on your Ingress. Exam tip. kube control describe ingress name lists the backend with its resolved endpoints; error endpoints x not found means the Service name or the Service itself is wrong.

1.title: Lab 15.1: ingress host routing
1.text: Lab fifteen point one: ingress host routing. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. An Ingress controller (Ingress Class traefik ) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing one, the Services a and b (port eighty) exist. Create an Ingress named routes that uses the class traefik and sends requests for the host a dot example dot com to the Service a and requests for the host b dot example dot com to the Service b, for all paths. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 15.1: ingress host routing, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get ingressclass. Then kube control dash n ing one create ingress routes the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to a dot example dot com or a eighty the rule flag set to b, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing one get ingress routes. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 15.2: ingress path routing
2.text: Lab fifteen point two: ingress path routing. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. An Ingress controller (Ingress Class traefik ) runs in the cluster. In the namespace ing five, the Services web and api (port eighty) exist. Create an Ingress named paths that uses the class traefik and serves the host app dot example dot com: requests for the path slash api (prefix) go to the Service api, and all other requests (the path or, prefix) go to the Service web. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 15.2: ingress path routing, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing five create ingress paths the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to app dot example dot com slash api api eighty the rule flag set to, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing five get ingress paths. Then sleep six. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 15.3: ingress tls
2.text: Lab fifteen point three: ingress tls. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace ing two, the Service a exists. A certificate and key for secure dot example dot com are in about slash answers slash tls dot crt and about slash answers slash tls dot key. Create a T L S Secret named web tls from them, and an Ingress named secure (class traefik ) that serves the host secure dot example dot com from the Service a on port eighty and uses the Secret for H T T P S. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 15.3: ingress tls, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing two create secret tls web tls the cert flag set to H O M E slash answers slash tls dot crt the key flag set to H O M, and so on. Then kube control dash n ing two create ingress secure the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to secure dot example dot com or a eighty,tls web tls. Then kube control dash n ing two get ingress secure. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 15.4: fix ingress class
2.text: Lab fifteen point four: fix ingress class. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace ing three, the Ingress site for the host site dot example dot com (backend Service a ) is not served: the controller answers four oh four. Find the cause and fix the Ingress (keep its name and rules) so that site dot example dot com returns the page of Service a. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 15.4: fix ingress class, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control get ingressclass. Then kube control dash n ing three get ingress site dash o json path dot spec dot ingress Class Name echo. Then kube control dash n ing three patch ingress site the type flag set to merge dash p spec ingress Class Name traefik. Then sleep six. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 15.5: fix ingress backend
2.text: Lab fifteen point five: fix ingress backend. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace ing four, requests for shop dot example dot com through the Ingress shop fail. The Service web is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Ingress so that shop dot example dot com returns the page of the Service web. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 15.5: fix ingress backend, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing four describe ingress shop then pipe to grep dash i -A two backend. Then kube control dash n ing four get svc. Then kube control dash n ing four patch ingress shop the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash rules slash zero slash http slash paths slash zero slash backend, and so on. Then sleep six. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 15.6: ingress default backend
2.text: Lab fifteen point six: ingress default backend. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. In the namespace ing six, the Services a and b (port eighty) exist. Create an Ingress named b route (class traefik ) that sends requests for the host b dot example dot com to the Service b, and a second Ingress named fallback (class traefik ) that has only a default backend ( default Backend ) pointing to the Service a, so that all other requests are answered by a. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 15.6: ingress default backend, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n ing six create ingress b route the class flag set to traefik the rule flag set to b dot example dot com or b eighty. Then kube control dash n ing six create ingress fallback the class flag set to traefik the default backend flag set to a eighty. Then kube control dash n ing six get ingress. Then sleep six. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the difference between an Ingress and an Ingress controller? Answer: The Ingress is the routing rule object; the controller is the program that reads it and routes the traffic. Question two. Which field links an Ingress to a controller? Answer: spec dot ingress Class Name. Question three. What does path Type Prefix with slash api match? Answer: slash api and every path below it, such as slash api slash users.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. In which namespace must the backend Service be? Answer: The same namespace as the Ingress. Question five. Which Secret type does Ingress T L S need? Answer: Kubernetes dot io slash tls with tls dot crt and tls dot key, in the Ingress's namespace. Question six. What does default Backend do? Answer: It receives the requests that match no rule.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What do you check first when every request returns four oh four? Answer: The Ingress Class name and the host in the Ingress. Question eight. Does a path rule rewrite the U R L? Answer: No; the backend receives the original path.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Parts: Ingress object (rules) plus controller (does the work); ingress Class Name. Rules: host, path, path Type (Prefix, Exact), backend dot service name plus port. Create: kube control create ingress name the class flag set to C the rule flag set to host slash path svc port. Default: default Backend for unmatched requests. T L S: kube control create secret tls; spec dot tls dot secret Name; same namespace. Longest path wins: slash api beats or. Debug: get ingressclass, describe ingress, get endpoints, Host header test. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
